Using \(\sin A = -\cos B = \sin(B-90^\circ)\),

\[
\sin 6x+\cos 4x=0
\]
\[
\sin 6x=-\cos 4x=\sin(4x-90^\circ).
\]

So
\[
\sin 6x=\sin(4x-90^\circ).
\]

This gives two cases:

1. \[
6x=4x-90^\circ+360^\circ k
\]
\[
2x=-90^\circ+360^\circ k
\]
\[
x=-45^\circ+180^\circ k
\]
In \([0^\circ,180^\circ)\), this gives \(x=135^\circ\).

2. \[
6x=180^\circ-(4x-90^\circ)+360^\circ k
\]
\[
6x=270^\circ-4x+360^\circ k
\]
\[
10x=270^\circ+360^\circ k
\]
\[
x=27^\circ+36^\circ k.
\]
For \(0^\circ\le x<180^\circ\), this gives
\[
27^\circ,63^\circ,99^\circ,135^\circ,171^\circ.
\]

Combining and removing duplicates:

The answer is \(27^\circ, 63^\circ, 99^\circ, 135^\circ, 171^\circ\).
